response.initial_request: There is a hot smell near the kitchen socket by the counter, and the socket face feels warm. Please arrange an inspection. I am not sure whether the socket is safe to use.

other_sections.Attachments: No attachments are available for this case.

events.body: Reported a hot, slightly burning smell near the kitchen counter socket. Nora says the socket face felt warm after a kettle had been plugged in; she has unplugged the kettle. No smoke or visible flame reported. Asked for an inspection.
Maintenance request NBL-020-01 created and assigned for review. Tenant contact preference on file is portal messaging.
Asked whether there is smoke, sparking, a continuing smell, or anyone currently at the property, and whether the relevant circuit can be identified without touching the socket.
No smoke or sparks seen. Smell remains faint. Nora is at home with her 10-year-old son. She does not know which breaker serves the kitchen and has not opened the consumer unit.
Forwarded the report and tenant's update. Asked for authority and preferred attendance arrangements, noting the reported warmth and continuing smell.

Asked Northbridge to keep costs controlled and said he could send his regular general handyman, Rowan Pike, to look at it. Did not specify an electrical qualification or authorize a particular repair.
Asked whether the smell has changed and requested that no appliance be reconnected to the affected socket while attendance is being arranged.
Smell is still faint. Nora confirms the kettle remains unplugged. She cannot confirm whether the socket is on the same circuit as the refrigerator; the refrigerator is running.

File note: through this time, no emergency-response guidance, referral, or decision has been communicated to the tenant in the case messages. No contact with emergency services or other emergency response is recorded.
Asked Rowan to attend today, inspect the kitchen socket area, and report what he finds before undertaking work. Elliot described Rowan as his regular handyman.
Confirmed he could attend between 13:00 and 15:00. Said his work is general property maintenance and he does not carry out fixed-wiring repairs.
Proposed Rowan's attendance window, described him as the landlord's handyman, and asked for consent to share the reported symptoms and access details with him.
Agreed to the visit and sharing those details. Nora will be present until 12:30, then leave to collect her son. She says her adult sister, Tessa, may be at the flat later but has not confirmed.
Sent the tenant-approved symptom summary and access window. Asked Rowan to report his observations before doing any work. The message does not include the tenant's unrelated account details.

Said he has a non-contact voltage pen and basic hand tools, but no electrical test equipment. He intends only a visual look and will not remove the socket face or alter wiring. Asked whether he should still attend.
Reiterated that Rowan should attend and report. Elliot has not given separate approval for an electrician's call-out or for electrical repairs.

Leaving shortly for school collection. The smell is not stronger, but the socket area still feels warm when she holds her hand near it; she has not touched the face again. No confirmation yet that Tessa will be present.

File note: tenant initially reported warmth by touch and has since described warmth near the socket without touching it. No photo, temperature reading, electrical test, or confirmation of circuit isolation is available.
At the property. Nora has left; no one has answered the door. Rowan has not entered and asks whether to wait, use landlord-held access, or leave.

Asked whether Rowan has authorization to use landlord-held keys in the tenant's absence and whether an electrician can be commissioned if the reported condition persists. No response reached; voicemail left.
Texted, 'Please have a look if you can get in; keep it to the socket and let me know.' The text does not say whether Rowan may use a key, and Rowan has not confirmed receiving or acting on it.
Says Tessa cannot attend after all. Nora is still away and expects to return around 16:30. She reports no smoke or alarm but cannot say whether the smell has changed since leaving.
Confirmed he did not enter because nobody answered and he had no clear access authorization. No inspection or isolation has taken place. He remains available until 15:00.

Summarized that the handyman has not inspected, cannot perform fixed-wiring repairs, and lacks clear permission to enter while the tenant is away. Asked for an immediate decision on authority, attendance, and electrical assessment; no reply yet.

Nora says she is back at the property. The faint smell is still noticeable near the counter, and she has not used the socket. She has not switched off any breaker; the refrigerator remains powered. She says she has received no emergency-response guidance. No one has inspected the socket, and the landlord's response to the authority request is still outstanding.

args.subject: Kitchen socket at 8 Brindlewick Row, Oakhollow, ZZ1 1ZZ - safety advice
args.body: Hi Nora, thank you for the updates. No one has inspected the socket yet, and the landlord has not yet authorised an electrician. I have passed this to our property manager as a safety matter. Until the socket is checked by a qualified person, please do not use it and keep the kettle and other appliances unplugged from it. If you see smoke, sparks or scorching, if the smell or heat gets stronger, or if you feel unsafe, leave the property with your son and call 999 straight away. Please don't open or touch the socket face. We will update you as soon as the property manager has a decision.

args.reason: Possible electrical fire hazard at the kitchen socket. No inspection has happened, the landlord has not authorised an electrician or access, and the tenant has had no emergency guidance until now.

handover_note.known: Property: 8 Brindlewick Row, Oakhollow, ZZ1 1ZZ. Tenant Nora Bell reported a hot burning smell and a warm socket face by the kitchen counter (events 1, 4). The smell persisted and the area still felt warm at 12:08 (event 17). At 16:42 the smell is still noticeable and she is home with her 10-year-old son (events 4, 25). The kettle is unplugged and the socket is unused, but no breaker has been switched off (event 25). Landlord Elliot Vane wants costs controlled and offered his general handyman Rowan Pike (event 6). Rowan does not do fixed-wiring repairs and has no electrical test equipment (events 11, 15). The landlord has not approved an electrician or electrical repairs (events 6, 16). Rowan attended at 13:06 but did not enter: nobody answered and he had no clear key authority (events 19, 23). The landlord's 13:27 text to Rowan is ambiguous on keys (event 21). The landlord has not answered our voicemail (event 20) or the 15:02 email asking for an immediate decision (event 24).
handover_note.conflicts: Landlord says 'have a look if you can get in' (event 21) but never authorised key use or an electrician (events 16, 20, 24). The handyman is not competent to assess fixed wiring (events 11, 15). Tenant reported warmth by touch and later by hand-near (event 18). No photo, reading or test exists. Events 9 and 25 show no emergency guidance was given to the tenant before now.
handover_note.done: Asked the tenant safety questions and asked her not to reconnect appliances (events 3, 7). Forwarded the report to the landlord and chased him by call and email (events 5, 20, 24). Obtained tenant consent to share details (event 13). Sent the tenant a safety update: do not use the socket, call 999 and leave if smoke, sparks or a stronger smell or heat appear. No contractor has been instructed or booked and no spend has been committed.
handover_note.needed: The property manager should phone the landlord urgently and get authority for a qualified electrician (NICEIC or equivalent) to attend today or as soon as possible. Rowan should not be relied on for this. Agree access arrangements with the tenant. Consider advising the tenant to isolate the circuit if it can be done safely, and consider whether the fire service should be involved. Record the landlord's decision. The agency's duty of care has been raised, because the tenant went about 8 hours with no emergency guidance.

args.summary: Escalated to the property manager as a safety case. A warm socket with a burning smell is still unassessed. The landlord has not authorised an electrician or key access, and the only attendee is an unqualified handyman who did not enter. I sent the tenant safety guidance as an update.
facts: Tenant reports a hot smell and a warm socket near the kitchen counter, still noticeable at 16:42 (events 1, 17, 25).
The handyman does not do fixed wiring and has no test equipment (events 11, 15).
The landlord has not approved an electrician or electrical repairs (events 6, 16).
The handyman did not enter because nobody answered and he had no clear key authority (events 19, 23).
The landlord has not replied to the call or the email asking for an immediate decision (events 20, 24).
The tenant had no emergency guidance until now (events 9, 25). A 10-year-old child is at the property (event 4).
conflicts: The landlord's text says 'have a look if you can get in' (event 21) but gives no key authority and no electrician approval (events 16, 20).
The handyman is not qualified for the electrical assessment the situation needs (events 11, 15).
missing: Landlord authority for a qualified electrician and for access.
Any electrical test, photo or temperature reading.
options_rejected: Ask the landlord again: already chased three times with no reply, and the safety risk needs a decision by the property manager.
Instruct a contractor: there is no landlord approval for an electrician.
Wait: the hazard is live and a delay is unsafe.
Rely on the handyman: not competent, and no access authority.
args.uncertainty: The real severity of the fault is unknown because nothing has been tested. The landlord's current whereabouts and intentions are unknown.
